q1.a: The chassis (frame) number consists of the car's body/model code and a unique serial — e.g. ZVW30-1234567 or AWS210-1234567 for Japanese cars. You'll find it in the registration certificate, on the body plate or in the listing.

q2.a: Depending on the records found: vehicle details, mileage history, auction dates, auction houses, LOT numbers, grades, statuses, photos from Japan, the auction sheet and QR verification.

q3.q: Does the report prove 100% whether the car had an accident?
q3.a: No. The report is based on available Japanese auction and related records. If an accident or repair was never recorded, it may not appear. We recommend combining it with a professional body and technical inspection.

q4.q: If nothing is found, does that mean the car is accident-free?
q4.a: No. It only means no matching records were found in the sources used. It is not a conclusion of “no accidents”, “no repairs” or “genuine mileage”.

q5.a: We show the mileage recorded at the car's auction entries on different dates in order — whether it grew over time, dropped below an earlier record or disagrees between records.

q6.q: Does a mileage discrepancy always mean tampering?
q6.a: Not necessarily. A drop or mismatch is a warning sign, but recording errors and other causes exist. Ask the seller for an explanation and verify with diagnostics and other documents.

q7.a: The original sheet created when a car enters an auction: key details, mileage, equipment, grade, a body diagram and marks for found damage and repairs. Structure and grading methods vary by auction house.

q8.a: It means the car wasn't sold at that particular auction. On its own, this is not a judgment about the car's quality.

q9.q: Does the report show the car's current technical condition?
q9.a: No. The report shows historical records. Repairs made after arriving in Mongolia and the current condition of the engine, battery, running gear and electronics should be checked separately with professional diagnostics.

q10.q: Do photos and auction sheets appear for every car?
q10.a: No. Photos, auction sheets and the number of records depend on what was found for that specific car — report length differs per car.

finalCta.heading: Check the history first, not just the price
finalCta.subheading: A 20,000₮ report won't remove every risk of buying a used car, but it adds information you can know before deciding.
finalCta.priceNote: After entering a valid chassis number, you pay and the PDF report is generated from the available records.

footerNote.text: TJ CAR reports are based on available Japanese auction and related historical records. Data availability differs per car; the absence of records is not a guarantee of no accidents, no repairs or unchanged mileage. Have the car professionally inspected before purchase.
